topic.title: Incremental utility of target-conditioned readout with pooled observed histories
topic.question: Under the frozen visible inputs and training protocol, does combining pooled_observed history representation with the current target-conditioned readout outperform both frozen source bests, especially pooled_observed, after controlling for extra capacity, redundant evidence and measured training/inference cost?
topic.hypothesis: Target-conditioned readout may expose predictive relationships beyond those already captured by pooled_observed, but the small recent target/context contrast and shared history-representation ancestry make redundancy plausible. Retain both frozen source bests as utility controls and compare target-conditioned versus target-independent readout with matched capacity and duplicated-evidence controls. An advantage over pooled_observed that survives these controls and repetition would support incremental utility; failure to beat that stronger source, or an advantage reproduced by target-independent capacity or duplicated evidence, would leave complementarity unsupported. Measure parameters and training/inference cost, and reserve the remaining budget for attribution, repetition and final assessment. The compact evidence establishes neither the mechanism nor novelty.
